Company Incorporation.shortDescription: Complete assistance incorporating private, public, one-person, and Section 8 companies with MCA filing.
Company Incorporation.longDescription: We manage end-to-end company incorporation — name approval, DIN/DSC, MOA/AOA drafting, and SPICe+ filing — for private, public, OPC, and Section 8 companies.
requirements: Identity and address proof of directors

process.title: Document Drafting
process.description: Prepare MOA, AOA, and SPICe+ forms.

process.title: Incorporation Filing
process.description: File with MCA and receive certificate.

faqs.question: Which company type suits a solo founder?
faqs.answer: A One Person Company (OPC) is designed for single-founder businesses.

faqs.question: What is a Section 8 company?
faqs.answer: A non-profit entity formed for charitable or social objectives.

faqs.question: How many directors are needed for a public company?
faqs.answer: A minimum of three directors is required.

LLP Registration.shortDescription: End-to-end LLP incorporation including name approval, agreement drafting, and MCA filings.
LLP Registration.longDescription: We handle designated partner identification, name reservation, LLP agreement drafting, and FiLLiP filing to get your LLP incorporated smoothly.

process.title: Name Reservation
process.description: Reserve the LLP name via RUN-LLP.

faqs.question: What is the minimum capital for an LLP?
faqs.answer: There is no minimum capital requirement.

faqs.question: Is LLP agreement filing time-bound?
faqs.answer: Yes, within 30 days of incorporation.

faqs.question: Can an LLP be converted to a company later?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to conditions under the Companies Act.

Company Name Approval.shortDescription: Assistance in selecting and reserving a suitable company name per MCA naming rules.
Company Name Approval.longDescription: We check name availability, ensure compliance with MCA naming guidelines, and file the name reservation application to secure your preferred name.
benefits: Avoids rejection due to naming conflicts

faqs.question: How long is an approved name valid?
faqs.answer: 20 days for a new company from the date of approval.

faqs.question: Can I reserve a name with a trademark?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you or your group owns the relevant trademark.

faqs.question: What if my name is rejected?
faqs.answer: You can resubmit with alternate names based on MCA feedback.

DIN Application.shortDescription: Assistance in obtaining a Director Identification Number for individuals proposed as company directors.
DIN Application.longDescription: DIN is a mandatory unique number for company directors. We manage documentation and application filing through SPICe+ or DIR-3 as applicable.

faqs.question: Is DIN required for every director?
faqs.answer: Yes, every director must hold a valid DIN.

faqs.question: Can one person hold multiple DINs?
faqs.answer: No, only one DIN per individual is permitted.

faqs.question: Does DIN expire?
faqs.answer: No, but annual KYC is mandatory to keep it active.

DSC Registration.shortDescription: Obtain Digital Signature Certificates required for signing MCA and other statutory e-filings.
DSC Registration.longDescription: DSC is required for directors and authorized signatories to digitally sign MCA forms. We manage application, verification, and issuance.

process.title: Issuance
process.description: Receive the DSC on a USB token.

faqs.question: How long is a DSC valid?
faqs.answer: Typically 1 to 3 years, depending on the type purchased.

faqs.question: Is Class 3 DSC mandatory for MCA filings?
faqs.answer: Yes, Class 3 is the standard requirement for most statutory filings.

faqs.question: Can DSC be used for GST filing too?
faqs.answer: Yes, the same Class 3 DSC can be used across GST, MCA, and Income Tax filings.

Director Appointment.shortDescription: Manage the appointment of new directors with board resolutions and MCA filing compliance.
Director Appointment.longDescription: We handle the complete process of appointing a new director, including board/shareholder approval, consent letters, and DIR-12 filing with MCA.
features: Board resolution and consent letter drafting
requirements: New director's identity/address proof and DIN

faqs.question: What is the filing deadline for director appointment?
faqs.answer: DIR-12 must be filed within 30 days of the appointment.

faqs.question: Does the new director need a DIN?
faqs.answer: Yes, a valid DIN is mandatory before appointment.

faqs.question: Is shareholder approval required?
faqs.answer: For certain appointments, such as beyond the maximum director limit, yes.

Director Resignation.shortDescription: Process director resignations with proper documentation and timely MCA filing.
Director Resignation.longDescription: We manage resignation letters, board acknowledgment, and DIR-12 filing to ensure the resignation is properly recorded and compliant.

process.title: Record Update
process.description: Update statutory registers and MCA master data.

faqs.question: Can a director resign independently?
faqs.answer: Yes, a director can resign by giving notice; the company should also file DIR-12.

faqs.question: What is the filing deadline?
faqs.answer: Within 30 days of the resignation being effective.

faqs.question: Does resignation absolve past liability?
faqs.answer: No, liability for the period served as director generally continues.

Director Removal.shortDescription: Manage the legal process of removing a director through shareholder resolution and MCA filing.
Director Removal.longDescription: Director removal requires following due process under the Companies Act, including special notice and shareholder resolution. We manage documentation and filing.
benefits: Reduces risk of wrongful removal claims

process.title: Notice & Meeting
process.description: Issue special notice and convene meeting.

process.title: Resolution
process.description: Pass the shareholder resolution for removal.

faqs.question: What is a special notice?
faqs.answer: A notice of at least 14 days required for removal resolutions.

faqs.question: Can a director contest removal?
faqs.answer: Yes, the director has a right to be heard at the meeting.

faqs.question: Is removal different from resignation?
faqs.answer: Yes, removal is an involuntary action initiated by shareholders.

Director KYC.shortDescription: Complete annual Director KYC filing to keep your DIN active and compliant.
Director KYC.longDescription: Every DIN holder must complete annual KYC via DIR-3 KYC to avoid deactivation. We manage the filing accurately and on time each year.

faqs.question: What is the due date for DIR-3 KYC?
faqs.answer: 30th September following the financial year.

faqs.question: What happens if KYC is missed?
faqs.answer: The DIN gets deactivated and a penalty applies for reactivation.

faqs.question: Is KYC needed every year?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is an annual compliance requirement for all DIN holders.

Annual MCA Compliance.shortDescription: Manage your company's complete annual MCA compliance calendar covering all mandatory filings.
Annual MCA Compliance.longDescription: We handle the full suite of annual compliances — AGM, financial statements, annual return, and director filings — ensuring nothing is missed.
benefits: Single point of annual compliance management

process.title: Documentation & Filing
process.description: Prepare and file each required form.

faqs.question: What are the key annual MCA filings?
faqs.answer: AOC-4 (financials), MGT-7 (annual return), and DIR-3 KYC, among others.

faqs.question: Is AGM mandatory for all companies?
faqs.answer: Most companies must hold an AGM, with some exemptions for OPCs.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late annual filing?
faqs.answer: ₹100 per day per form, with no upper cap.

Financial Statement Filing.shortDescription: Prepare and file your company's financial statements with MCA through Form AOC-4.
Financial Statement Filing.longDescription: We compile and file audited financial statements, board's report, and auditor's report through AOC-4 within the prescribed timeline.

faqs.question: What is the due date for AOC-4?
faqs.answer: Within 30 days of the AGM.

faqs.question: Is XBRL filing mandatory for all companies?
faqs.answer: No, only for specified classes of companies like listed and large companies.

faqs.question: What happens on late filing?
faqs.answer: A daily additional fee applies until the form is filed.

Annual Return Filing.shortDescription: Preparation and filing of the company's annual return with MCA through Form MGT-7.
Annual Return Filing.longDescription: We compile shareholding, director, and compliance details to prepare and file an accurate annual return within the statutory deadline.

process.title: Filing
process.description: Submit the annual return to MCA.

faqs.question: What is the due date for MGT-7?
faqs.answer: Within 60 days of the AGM.

faqs.question: What is MGT-7A?
faqs.answer: A simplified annual return form for small companies and OPCs.

faqs.question: Is annual return different from financial statements?
faqs.answer: Yes, it covers shareholding and governance data, not financial figures.

Company Master Data Correction.shortDescription: Correct errors in your company's master data on the MCA portal, such as address or contact details.
Company Master Data Correction.longDescription: Incorrect master data can cause filing rejections and compliance issues. We identify the discrepancy and file the appropriate correction request with the RoC.

process.title: Discrepancy Review
process.description: Identify the incorrect master data field.

process.title: Application Filing
process.description: File correction request with the RoC.

faqs.question: What common errors need correction?
faqs.answer: Incorrect email, address, or authorized capital figures, among others.

faqs.question: Can this be corrected through self-service?
faqs.answer: Some fields require a formal application to the RoC.

faqs.question: How long does correction take?
faqs.answer: Typically 2-4 weeks depending on RoC processing time.

Registered Office Change.shortDescription: Manage your company's registered office change with proper board approval and MCA filing.
Registered Office Change.longDescription: Whether within the same city or across states, we handle the required resolutions, filings (INC-22/INC-23), and RoC coordination for office address change.
requirements: NOC from property owner, if applicable

process.title: Approval
process.description: Pass board/shareholder resolution for the change.

faqs.question: Is regional director approval needed?
faqs.answer: Yes, for change of registered office between states.

faqs.question: What is the filing deadline?
faqs.answer: INC-22 must be filed within 30 days of the change.

faqs.question: Does PAN/GST need updating too?
faqs.answer: Yes, related registrations should be updated with the new address.

Object Clause Modification.shortDescription: Amend your company's main object clause to reflect new or expanded business activities.
Object Clause Modification.longDescription: Changing your business activities requires amending the MOA's object clause through shareholder approval and MCA filing.

process.title: Resolution
process.description: Pass the special resolution at general meeting.

faqs.question: Is special resolution mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, object clause changes require a 75% shareholder majority.

faqs.question: Can objects be expanded and restricted?
faqs.answer: Yes, both addition and removal of objects can be done through this process.

faqs.question: Is RoC approval required?
faqs.answer: The resolution filing itself completes the process; no separate approval is generally needed.

MOA Amendment.shortDescription: Amend your Memorandum of Association covering name, objects, capital, or registered office clauses.
MOA Amendment.longDescription: MOA amendments require proper resolutions and MCA filings depending on the clause being changed. We manage documentation and filing for a compliant amendment.

process.title: Filing
process.description: File the applicable form with MCA.

faqs.question: What clauses can be amended?
faqs.answer: Name, registered office, objects, capital, and liability clauses.

faqs.question: Does every amendment need special resolution?
faqs.answer: Most do, though some capital-related changes may need only ordinary resolution.

faqs.question: Is Central Government approval ever needed?
faqs.answer: Rarely, mainly for specific name change or object restrictions.

AOA Amendment.shortDescription: Amend your Articles of Association to update internal governance rules and provisions.
AOA Amendment.longDescription: AOA amendments update internal governance rules like director powers, share transfer restrictions, or meeting procedures. We handle drafting and filing.

faqs.question: What is commonly amended in AOA?
faqs.answer: Share transfer restrictions, director appointment rights, and meeting procedures.

faqs.question: Is shareholder approval required?
faqs.answer: Yes, via special resolution with 75% majority.

faqs.question: Can AOA override the Companies Act?
faqs.answer: No, AOA provisions must be consistent with the Companies Act.

Authorized Capital Increase.shortDescription: Increase your company's authorized share capital through resolution and MCA filing.
Authorized Capital Increase.longDescription: We manage the process of increasing authorized capital, including MOA amendment, resolution drafting, and SH-7 filing with the applicable government fee.

process.title: Filing
process.description: File SH-7 with MCA and pay fees.

faqs.question: What is authorized vs paid-up capital?
faqs.answer: Authorized is the maximum capital a company can issue; paid-up is what's actually issued.

faqs.question: Is there a fee for increasing capital?
faqs.answer: Yes, government fee based on the incremental capital amount.

faqs.question: Does this require shareholder approval?
faqs.answer: Yes, typically via ordinary resolution unless AOA specifies otherwise.

Share Transfer Compliance.shortDescription: Ensure compliant share transfer documentation and MCA/statutory register updates.
Share Transfer Compliance.longDescription: We prepare share transfer deeds, verify board approval requirements, and update statutory registers to ensure a legally valid transfer.

process.title: Approval & Stamping
process.description: Obtain board approval and stamp the deed.

faqs.question: Is board approval mandatory for share transfer?
faqs.answer: Yes, for private companies, unless AOA states otherwise.

faqs.question: Is stamp duty applicable on transfer?
faqs.answer: Yes, as per applicable state stamp duty rates.

faqs.question: Can share transfer be restricted?
faqs.answer: Yes, private companies often have transfer restrictions in their AOA.

Share Allotment Filing.shortDescription: Manage new share allotment with proper board approval and PAS-3 filing with MCA.
Share Allotment Filing.longDescription: Whether for fresh capital or ESOPs, we manage resolution drafting, allotment documentation, and timely PAS-3 filing with MCA.
features: Allotment letter and share certificate preparation

faqs.question: What is the filing deadline for PAS-3?
faqs.answer: Within 30 days of allotment.

faqs.question: Is valuation required for allotment?
faqs.answer: Yes, particularly for allotment to non-shareholders or above face value.

faqs.question: Are share certificates mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, must be issued within 2 months of allotment.

Share Capital Reduction.shortDescription: Manage the legal process of reducing company share capital through NCLT-approved procedures.
Share Capital Reduction.longDescription: Capital reduction requires shareholder approval and NCLT confirmation. We manage documentation, filings, and coordination through the entire process.

process.title: Resolution & Scheme
process.description: Pass resolution and prepare reduction scheme.

process.title: NCLT Filing
process.description: File petition and obtain creditor consents.

process.title: Confirmation & Filing
process.description: Obtain NCLT order and file with MCA.

faqs.question: Is NCLT approval always required?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, except for specific exempted cases.

faqs.question: Why reduce share capital?
faqs.answer: To write off losses, return excess capital, or restructure the balance sheet.

faqs.question: Do creditors need to consent?
faqs.answer: Yes, creditor no-objection is typically required before NCLT confirmation.

Charge Creation.shortDescription: Register charges on company assets created in favor of lenders through CHG-1 filing.
Charge Creation.longDescription: When a company borrows against assets, the charge must be registered with MCA. We manage documentation and timely CHG-1 filing to perfect the security.

faqs.question: What is the filing deadline for charge creation?
faqs.answer: Within 30 days of creation, extendable with additional fees.

faqs.question: What happens if a charge isn't registered?
faqs.answer: It becomes void against the liquidator and other creditors.

faqs.question: Is charge registration only for banks?
faqs.answer: No, it applies to any charge created on company assets, including from NBFCs or private lenders.

Charge Modification.shortDescription: Update registered charge details following changes in loan terms or security arrangements.
Charge Modification.longDescription: Modifications to charge amount, terms, or details require filing with MCA. We manage documentation and CHG-1 (modification) filing accurately.
benefits: Keeps charge records accurate and current
Avoids compliance gaps from outdated filings

faqs.question: What triggers a charge modification filing?
faqs.answer: Changes in loan amount, interest rate, or security terms.

faqs.question: Is the filing deadline the same as creation?
faqs.answer: Yes, generally within 30 days of the modification.

faqs.question: Can multiple modifications be filed over time?
faqs.answer: Yes, each change requires a separate filing.

Charge Satisfaction.shortDescription: File charge satisfaction with MCA once the underlying loan or security obligation is fully repaid.
Charge Satisfaction.longDescription: After loan repayment, the registered charge must be marked as satisfied with MCA. We manage documentation and CHG-4 filing to close the encumbrance.
benefits: Improves ability to raise fresh finance

process.title: Confirmation
process.description: Obtain no-dues certificate from the lender.

faqs.question: What is the filing deadline for satisfaction?
faqs.answer: Within 30 days of full repayment/satisfaction.

faqs.question: What if satisfaction isn't filed?
faqs.answer: The charge remains on record, potentially affecting future financing.

faqs.question: Is lender confirmation mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, to support the satisfaction claim before the RoC.

Company Strike Off.shortDescription: Voluntarily close down an inactive company through the fast-track strike-off process with MCA.
Company Strike Off.longDescription: For companies with no operations, strike-off offers a simpler closure route than liquidation. We manage documentation, board approval, and STK-2 filing.

process.title: Approval
process.description: RoC processes and strikes off the company.

faqs.question: Which companies are eligible for strike-off?
faqs.answer: Companies with no business activity for the preceding two financial years, among other conditions.

faqs.question: Are pending liabilities allowed?
faqs.answer: No, all liabilities must be cleared before applying.

faqs.question: Can a struck-off company be revived?
faqs.answer: Yes, through NCLT within a specified period.

Company Revival.shortDescription: Restore a struck-off company's status through NCLT application and compliance catch-up.
Company Revival.longDescription: A struck-off company can be revived through NCLT within the permitted period. We manage the petition, compliance catch-up, and RoC restoration process.

process.title: Case Preparation
process.description: Prepare grounds and petition for revival.

process.title: Restoration
process.description: Obtain order and restore company status.

faqs.question: What is the time limit for revival?
faqs.answer: Generally within 20 years of the strike-off, though sooner is preferable.

faqs.question: Who can file for revival?
faqs.answer: The company, member, creditor, or workman can apply.

faqs.question: Are pending filings required post-revival?
faqs.answer: Yes, all overdue compliances must be completed after restoration.

Company Conversion.shortDescription: Convert your company's structure — such as private to LLP or company type changes — with full compliance.
Company Conversion.longDescription: We manage conversions between business structures, handling resolutions, NOCs, and RoC filings required for a smooth, compliant transition.
benefits: Compliant handling of assets and liabilities

faqs.question: What types of conversions are common?
faqs.answer: Private to public, LLP to company, and partnership to company, among others.

faqs.question: Does conversion trigger new PAN/TAN?
faqs.answer: Depends on the type; some conversions retain the same PAN.

faqs.question: Are existing contracts affected?
faqs.answer: Generally contracts continue, though assignment clauses should be reviewed.

Private to Public Conversion.shortDescription: Convert your private limited company to a public company with complete MCA compliance.
Private to Public Conversion.longDescription: We manage the special resolution, AOA amendment, and RoC filing required to convert your private company into a public company.
features: AOA amendment for public company norms

faqs.question: What is the minimum director requirement?
faqs.answer: At least three directors for a public company.

faqs.question: Does the name change on conversion?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Private' is removed from the company name.

faqs.question: Are compliance requirements higher after conversion?
faqs.answer: Yes, public companies face more extensive governance and disclosure norms.

Public to Private Conversion.shortDescription: Convert your public company to a private company with NCLT and MCA compliance.
Public to Private Conversion.longDescription: We manage the special resolution, NCLT approval where required, and RoC filing for converting a public company to private status.

faqs.question: Is NCLT approval always required?
faqs.answer: Yes, in most cases of public to private conversion.

faqs.question: What changes in the AOA?
faqs.answer: Share transfer restrictions and reduced member limits are added.

faqs.question: Does the company name change?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Private' is added to the company name.

Company Merger & Amalgamation.shortDescription: Manage the legal process of merging or amalgamating companies through NCLT-sanctioned schemes.
Company Merger & Amalgamation.longDescription: We handle scheme drafting, NCLT filing, and post-sanction compliance for company mergers and amalgamations, ensuring a legally sound combination.

process.title: Post-Sanction Compliance
process.description: File the sanctioned order and update records.

faqs.question: Is NCLT approval mandatory for all mergers?
faqs.answer: Most mergers require NCLT sanction, with a simplified process for small companies.

faqs.question: How long does the process take?
faqs.answer: Typically 6-12 months depending on complexity and objections.

faqs.question: What happens to employees post-merger?
faqs.answer: Generally, employment terms continue under the surviving entity as per the scheme.

Demerger & Corporate Restructuring.shortDescription: Manage demerger and corporate restructuring transactions through NCLT-approved schemes.
Demerger & Corporate Restructuring.longDescription: We assist with structuring and executing demergers to separate business divisions, managing scheme drafting, NCLT filing, and compliance.
benefits: Clear allocation of assets and liabilities
requirements: Financial statements of the demerging entity

process.title: Scheme Structuring
process.description: Design the demerger scheme and terms.

process.title: NCLT Proceedings
process.description: File petition and conduct required meetings.

process.title: Post-Sanction Compliance
process.description: Implement scheme and update statutory records.

faqs.question: What is a demerger?
faqs.answer: Separation of one or more undertakings into a distinct company.

faqs.question: Is demerger tax-neutral?
faqs.answer: Only if it satisfies specific conditions under the Income Tax Act.

faqs.question: Is shareholder approval needed?
faqs.answer: Yes, along with NCLT sanction of the scheme.

Section 8 Company Compliance.shortDescription: Ensure ongoing compliance for Section 8 (non-profit) companies covering filings and license conditions.
Section 8 Company Compliance.longDescription: Section 8 companies have specific compliance obligations tied to their license conditions. We manage annual filings and compliance monitoring.

process.title: Compliance Review
process.description: Assess license conditions and filing needs.

faqs.question: Can Section 8 companies distribute profits?
faqs.answer: No, profits must be applied to promoting the company's objects.

faqs.question: What happens on non-compliance?
faqs.answer: The Central Government can revoke the Section 8 license.

faqs.question: Is CSR applicable to Section 8 companies?
faqs.answer: It can apply to Section 8 companies meeting the CSR applicability thresholds.

Producer Company Compliance.shortDescription: Manage statutory compliance requirements specific to producer companies under the Companies Act.
Producer Company Compliance.longDescription: Producer companies have unique governance and reporting requirements. We handle annual filings, member records, and board compliance tailored to this structure.

faqs.question: Who can be a member of a producer company?
faqs.answer: Primary producers such as farmers or producer institutions.

faqs.question: Is profit distribution restricted?
faqs.answer: Distribution follows patronage-based principles unique to producer companies.

faqs.question: Are annual filings similar to regular companies?
faqs.answer: Broadly similar, with additional producer-specific disclosures.

Nidhi Company Compliance.shortDescription: Manage compliance obligations specific to Nidhi companies including NDH forms and member limits.
Nidhi Company Compliance.longDescription: Nidhi companies must meet specific membership, deposit, and lending ratios along with dedicated NDH form filings. We manage this specialized compliance.

faqs.question: What is NDH-1?
faqs.answer: A return of statutory compliance filed within 90 days of the financial year.

faqs.question: What happens on non-compliance with ratios?
faqs.answer: The company must seek an extension or risk regulatory action.

faqs.question: Can Nidhi companies accept deposits from the public?
faqs.answer: No, only from their members.

One Person Company Compliance.shortDescription: Manage annual and event-based compliance requirements specific to One Person Companies.
One Person Company Compliance.longDescription: OPCs enjoy simplified compliance but still have mandatory filings. We manage annual returns, financial statements, and nominee-related documentation.

faqs.question: Is AGM mandatory for OPCs?
faqs.answer: No, OPCs are exempt from holding an AGM.

faqs.question: Is a nominee mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, every OPC must nominate a person in case of the sole member's incapacity.

faqs.question: Can an OPC convert to a private company?
faqs.answer: Yes, voluntarily or mandatorily upon crossing prescribed thresholds.

Board Meeting Compliance.shortDescription: Manage board meeting notices, agendas, minutes, and compliance under the Companies Act.
Board Meeting Compliance.longDescription: We help schedule, document, and record board meetings in compliance with statutory requirements, ensuring proper notice periods and minute-keeping.

process.title: Notice Preparation
process.description: Draft and circulate meeting notice and agenda.

faqs.question: How many board meetings are required annually?
faqs.answer: At least four, with a maximum gap of 120 days between meetings.

faqs.question: What is the notice period for a board meeting?
faqs.answer: At least 7 days, unless shortened with proper consent.

faqs.question: Are minutes mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, minutes must be recorded and maintained for every meeting.

General Meeting Compliance.shortDescription: Manage AGM and EGM compliance including notices, resolutions, and statutory filings.
General Meeting Compliance.longDescription: We handle the complete general meeting process — notice drafting, resolution preparation, and post-meeting MGT-14 filing where applicable.

process.title: Notice Preparation
process.description: Draft and circulate the meeting notice.

process.title: Filing
process.description: File resolutions with MCA, if required.

faqs.question: What is the deadline to hold an AGM?
faqs.answer: Within 6 months of the financial year end (9 months for the first AGM).

faqs.question: What is an EGM?
faqs.answer: An Extraordinary General Meeting called for urgent matters outside the AGM.

faqs.question: Which resolutions require MGT-14 filing?
faqs.answer: Special resolutions and certain board resolutions specified under the Act.

Board Resolution Drafting.shortDescription: Professional drafting of board resolutions for various corporate approvals and decisions.
Board Resolution Drafting.longDescription: We draft precise, legally sound board resolutions for matters ranging from bank account opening to major corporate approvals, ensuring proper authority is documented.
benefits: Reduces rejection risk from generic templates

process.title: Requirement Review
process.description: Understand the purpose and scope needed.

process.title: Drafting
process.description: Prepare the resolution with correct format.

process.title: Finalization
process.description: Finalize for board approval and signature.

faqs.question: What are common resolution purposes?
faqs.answer: Bank account opening, loan approval, director appointment, and contract authorization.

faqs.question: Do resolutions need to be filed with MCA?
faqs.answer: Only specific resolutions require filing; most are for internal/bank records.

faqs.question: Can a resolution be passed by circulation?
faqs.answer: Yes, for certain matters not requiring a physical meeting.

Corporate Registers & Records.shortDescription: Maintain statutory registers and records required under the Companies Act.
Corporate Registers & Records.longDescription: We set up and maintain statutory registers — members, directors, charges, and more — ensuring your company meets its record-keeping obligations.

faqs.question: What registers are mandatory?
faqs.answer: Register of members, directors, charges, and contracts, among others.

faqs.question: Can registers be maintained electronically?
faqs.answer: Yes, electronic maintenance is permitted under prescribed conditions.

faqs.question: Who can inspect these registers?
faqs.answer: Members, and in certain cases, regulatory authorities.

MCA Notice & Reply.shortDescription: Professional preparation of responses to notices issued by the Registrar of Companies.
MCA Notice & Reply.longDescription: MCA/RoC notices require timely, accurate responses. We review the notice, prepare supporting documentation, and file a comprehensive reply.
benefits: Reduces risk of adverse RoC action

process.title: Notice Review
process.description: Understand the issue raised by RoC.

faqs.question: What triggers an RoC notice?
faqs.answer: Non-filing, discrepancies, or compliance verification checks.

faqs.question: What happens if unanswered?
faqs.answer: It may lead to penalty proceedings or company status change.

faqs.question: Can penalties be reduced with a good response?
faqs.answer: A well-documented response can support leniency in some cases.

MCA Compounding & Adjudication.shortDescription: Manage compounding applications and adjudication proceedings for MCA compliance defaults.
MCA Compounding & Adjudication.longDescription: For technical defaults, compounding offers a way to settle violations without prolonged litigation. We manage applications and represent before adjudicating officers.

process.title: Default Assessment
process.description: Identify and quantify the compliance default.

faqs.question: What is compounding of offences?
faqs.answer: A process to settle certain company law offences by paying a prescribed sum.

faqs.question: Are all offences compoundable?
faqs.answer: No, only those not punishable with imprisonment only or above specified severity.

faqs.question: What is adjudication?
faqs.answer: A quasi-judicial process where the RoC imposes penalties for specified defaults.

Corporate Secretarial Audit Support.shortDescription: Support for secretarial audits ensuring compliance with the Companies Act and related regulations.
Corporate Secretarial Audit Support.longDescription: We assist in preparing documentation and coordinating with the practicing company secretary for a smooth, comprehensive secretarial audit.

faqs.question: Who requires a secretarial audit?
faqs.answer: Listed companies and other prescribed classes of companies.

faqs.question: What does the audit cover?
faqs.answer: Compliance with the Companies Act, SEBI regulations, and other applicable laws.

faqs.question: What happens on audit qualifications?
faqs.answer: They must be explained in the board's report and addressed going forward.

Dormant Company Status.shortDescription: Apply for dormant company status to reduce compliance burden for inactive companies.
Dormant Company Status.longDescription: Companies with no significant transactions can apply for dormant status, reducing compliance obligations while retaining legal existence. We manage the MSC-1 application.
benefits: Retains legal existence for future use

faqs.question: What qualifies as a dormant company?
faqs.answer: A company formed for future projects or with no significant transactions.

faqs.question: Is any compliance still required?
faqs.answer: Yes, minimal annual filings (MSC-3) are still required.

faqs.question: How long can a company remain dormant?
faqs.answer: Up to 5 consecutive years, after which status must be reviewed.

Foreign Company Registration.shortDescription: Register your foreign company's branch, liaison, or project office in India with MCA compliance.
Foreign Company Registration.longDescription: We manage the registration of foreign company establishments in India, including RBI approval coordination and MCA filing under Section 380.
benefits: Legal establishment for foreign entities in India
Compliant entry into the Indian market

process.title: MCA Filing
process.description: File FC-1 for registration in India.

faqs.question: What is the difference between branch and liaison office?
faqs.answer: Branch offices can conduct business; liaison offices can only represent and communicate.

faqs.question: Is RBI approval always required?
faqs.answer: Yes, for establishing any place of business in India by a foreign company.

faqs.question: What ongoing compliance applies?
faqs.answer: Annual filings including FC-3 and FC-4 with MCA.

Foreign Investment Compliance.shortDescription: Ensure compliance with FEMA and RBI requirements for foreign investment into Indian companies.
Foreign Investment Compliance.longDescription: We manage reporting and compliance for foreign direct investment, including sector eligibility checks, FC-GPR filing, and valuation compliance.
features: Sector cap and route eligibility check

process.title: Filing
process.description: File FC-GPR on the FIRMS portal.

faqs.question: What is FC-GPR?
faqs.answer: A report filed when shares are allotted against foreign investment.

faqs.question: Is all FDI under automatic route?
faqs.answer: No, some sectors require prior government approval.

faqs.question: What is the filing deadline for FC-GPR?
faqs.answer: Within 30 days of share allotment.
